checks.source: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/merchant-listing (required: name, image, offers with price and priceCurrency; recommended: description, sku, brand.name, offers.availability)
checks.applicability: Applies to JSON-LD nodes of type Product on a purchasable product detail page in the audited document (top level, top-level arrays, @graph entries; full schema.org IRIs count as the short type). Microdata and RDFa are outside this method.
checks.expectation: Applies only where the page is a purchasable product detail page; the audit establishes that from the visible page intent (shop) and the product route in the SEO module's derive step. Where that context is not established the Product gets needs_review (context unknown), never a pass or a violation. On a product detail page: fails when name, image or an Offer with price and priceCurrency is missing; with them present and recommended properties missing it is needs_review (Google's Rich Results Test reports missing recommended properties as non-critical issues (eligible, but a human should decide whether the data exists)); all present passes. Nested property values (an author Person, a provider Organization) are not nodes of their own and are not assessed; a page without a node of the type is not applicable. A page whose structured-data collection fails is not run for every feature, never clean.
